clue.text: Week-end winter sport enthusiast decidedly more perky

parts.note: Friday, FRI, is the end of the working week
a skier is a fan of the classic winter sport

explanation.surface: A weekend skier is noticeably livelier than usual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Week-end' looks like Saturday and Sunday, but here it is the day that ends the working week, abbreviated FRI.
explanation.definitionFit: Frisky means lively and playful, so the comparative is a plain synonym of being more perky.

clue.text: Lining ripped out of female explorer's hat

indicators.note: with the lining ripped out, only the outside letters of female remain

parts.note: Dora the Explorer is the children's cartoon character

explanation.surface: The lining has been torn from a female explorer's hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat with a creased crown, worn by Indiana Jones.

clue.text: Threaten current elected politician on purpose

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
an MP is an elected Member of Parliament
an end is a goal or purpose

explanation.surface: Someone deliberately threatens the sitting MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On purpose' reads as 'deliberately', but 'on' is just a link and 'purpose' gives END.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that impends is about to happen, looming over us as a threat.

clue.text: Ford making two circuits of roundabout in the city

parts.note: the Ka is a small Ford car

indicators.note: in tells us the roundabout's letter goes inside

parts.note: going round twice, so TWICE
O is round in shape, like a roundabout

explanation.surface: A Ford car goes twice round a roundabout in town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ford' is a car model here, not a river crossing.
explanation.definitionFit: Katowice is an industrial city in southern Poland.

clue.text: All heads of Europe attract considerable hostility

indicators.note: heads of means the first letter of every one of the four following words

explanation.surface: All the leaders of Europe draw a great deal of hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads of Europe' reads as political leaders but means initial letters.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'a pound all' or 'a pound each', all can mean apiece.

clue.text: Navy flier circling Sandhurst area

indicators.note: circling means the flier's letters go round the academy's letters

parts.note: a flier is a leaflet or advertisement, AD
Sandhurst is the Royal Military Academy, RMA, Britain's officer-training college

explanation.surface: A navy aircraft flies in circles over the military academy at Sandhurst.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flier' suggests an aircraft beside 'Navy', but it is a printed leaflet. Sandhurst is the British Army's officer academy.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a fleet of warships, which is what a navy is.

clue.text: Currency run on yen drained reserves

parts.note: the rand is South Africa's currency
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: A currency run on the yen drains a country's reserves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yen' reads as a currency alongside 'run', the run on a currency, but each gives just a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To run dry is to exhaust a supply, which is what draining reserves does.

clue.text: Got intro of Argentinian tango rehearsed right away

indicators.note: the intro of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: Tango is the NATO alphabet word for T

indicators.note: away tells us right is sent away from the rehearsed word

parts.note: rehearsed means trained or drilled

explanation.surface: An Argentine dancer learns the tango after rehearsing straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right away' looks like 'immediately' but splits into R and its deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To have attained something is to have reached or got it.

clue.text: A bit of Bach in G, lyrical in an excruciating way

indicators.note: a bit of means only a piece lifted from within these words

explanation.surface: A Bach piece in G, played lyrically, is painfully moving.
explanation.definitionFit: Achingly means so intensely it hurts, which is excruciatingly.

clue.text: Rodney say, giving guacamole and hummus the thumbs-up?

parts.note: both are dips served with crisps or bread
a tick is a mark of approval, like a thumbs-up

explanation.surface: Rodney gives his approval to the guacamole and hummus at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Rodney Trotter of the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses is routinely called a dipstick, a fool, by his brother Del Boy.
explanation.definitionFit: Rodney is the best-known example of a dipstick, British slang for an idiot.

clue.text: Grab tin 'elmet — church needs evacuating

parts.note: Sn is the chemical symbol for tin
'elmet is helmet with its H dropped, so hat with its H dropped gives AT

indicators.note: evacuating empties the word church of its inside letters, leaving its outer pair

explanation.surface: A cockney-voiced instruction to snatch a tin helmet while the church is cleared.
explanation.walkthrough: The dropped H of ''elmet' tells you to drop the H from a synonym too: helmet is a kind of hat, and 'at is what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To snatch something is to grab it quickly.

clue.text: Aircraft carrying German bailed out somewhere in Provence

indicators.note: carrying means the aircraft holds the German's letters inside it

parts.note: avion is French for aeroplane, apt for Provence

indicators.note: bailed out means emptied, leaving only the outer letters of German

explanation.surface: An aircraft with a German on board, who parachutes out over Provence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bailed out' reads as parachuting, but here it empties the word German to G and N.
explanation.definitionFit: Avignon is a historic city in Provence, seat of the popes in the 14th century.

clue.text: New owner, new reputation

indicators.note: new tells us the word owner is made fresh, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A new owner brings a business a new reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: Renown is fame or a good name, which is what a reputation is.

clue.text: Confirms retiring number one getting hostility

parts.note: to aver is to affirm or confirm

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the number and the one are read in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A departing chief executive's behaviour confirms a feeling of hostility.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number one' reads like a boss; it is split into NO and I, and 'retiring' reverses them to ION.
explanation.definitionFit: An aversion is a strong dislike, close in sense to hostility.

clue.text: Grow old, regularly missing extra aparting

definitions.note: read as 'a parting', a noun phrase for the farewell word

indicators.note: every other letter of these words is skipped, keeping the rest

parts.note: a bye is a run scored as an extra in cricket

explanation.surface: Growing old, one regularly misses extra time with loved ones before parting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aparting' is the clue as printed, to be read as 'a parting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodbye is the word said at a parting, and a goodbye can mean the farewell itself.

clue.text: Bloke under the influence of spirits creosoting draining can, drunk

definitions.text: Bloke under the influence of spirits

indicators.note: drunk means the remaining letters reel about into a new order
draining means the can is taken out of the word creosoting

parts.note: a can is a tin

explanation.surface: A drunk man is creosoting a fence after emptying a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under the influence of spirits' suggests drink, but means Dickens's miser, visited by three ghosts in A Christmas Carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrooge is the man changed by visiting ghosts, so the spirits here are supernatural ones.

clue.text: Five, 4 beginning to love meat

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
4 refers to the answer at 4-down, EACH, abbreviated EA

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cryptic list of numbers leading into the love of a certain meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference '4' points to the answer EACH, used in its abbreviated form ea.
explanation.definitionFit: Veal is the flesh of a calf eaten as meat.

clue.text: Where to get a burger, beer? (Cuba brewed)

indicators.note: brewed means the letters are stirred up and mixed into a new form

explanation.surface: Where to find a burger and a beer, with Cuban brew on the side.
explanation.definitionFit: A barbecue is an outdoor grill, the classic place for cooking a burger.

clue.text: Case of extreme importance coming up in Lincoln

indicators.note: in places the reversed word inside the president's name

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln's nickname

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from the bottom up, reversed

parts.note: vital means of extreme importance

explanation.surface: A case of great importance comes up in Lincoln, the English city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' looks like a legal matter but is grammatical. Lincoln suggests the English city, but it is the president.
explanation.definitionFit: The ablative is a grammatical case in Latin, marking means or separation.

clue.text: Bloody bow falls over, catching American campaigner!

indicators.note: catching means the reversed letters take the American inside
falls over means the pair is upended, read backwards

parts.note: bloody things are red
a bow is curved like an arc

explanation.surface: A bloodied bow falls over and traps an American fighter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' and 'bow' suggest medieval battle, apt for a crusader.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusader is someone who campaigns vigorously for a cause.

clue.text: Swedish foursome swings both ways

indicators.note: swings both ways says the group's name reads the same in either direction

parts.note: the Swedish pop quartet

explanation.surface: A Swedish pop quartet is said to be bisexual.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swings both ways' is slang for bisexual, but here it says the name is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: ABBA were the four-member Swedish pop group famous for Waterloo, and the name is a palindrome.

clue.text: Suspend boring Grauniad journalist

indicators.note: boring means the answer drills through the inside of these words

explanation.surface: A dull reporter from the Guardian is suspended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' reads as dull but means burrowing inside the words. The Grauniad is a jokey British name for the Guardian newspaper, mocking its typos.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjourn a meeting is to suspend it until later.

clue.text: Spare family housed in southern state

indicators.note: housed in means the family is lodged within the other letters

parts.note: NY is New York State
kin are one's family

explanation.surface: A spare room for family housed in a southern US state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare' looks like extra, as in a spare room, but means thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare can describe a lean, thin frame, which is skinny.

clue.text: Son no. 1 tackling a distant expedition

indicators.note: tackling means grappling with, so the son and number one wrap round the other words

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one, also first person
distant means far

explanation.surface: The eldest son takes on a far-flung expedition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Son no. 1' reads as the first-born, but splits into S and I.
explanation.definitionFit: A safari is an overland expedition, usually to see wild animals.

clue.text: Pull on reefer held by senior crewman

indicators.note: held by means the pull goes inside the senior letters

parts.note: a toke is a drag on a cannabis cigarette, or reefer

explanation.surface: A senior crewman is caught taking a drag on a joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reefer' has a nautical sense, a sailor reefing sails, which fits 'crewman', but here it is a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoker is a crew member who tended a ship's furnaces.

clue.text: British manservant finishing off Windolene shiner

parts.note: a lackey is a male servant

indicators.note: the finish of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A British butler finishes off the windows with Windolene to make them shine.
explanation.walkthrough: Windolene is a British window-cleaning spray, which makes 'shiner' seem to be about glass.
explanation.definitionFit: A shiner is slang for a bruised eye after a punch.

clue.text: Time to pursue character from Lewis sloping off

indicators.note: to pursue means come after, so the time follows the character

parts.note: Aslan is the lion in C. S. Lewis's Narnia books

explanation.surface: Time to follow a Lewis character who is sneaking away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To pursue' puts T after the lion. 'Lewis' might suggest the Scottish isle, but it is the Narnia author.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslant means at a slant, tilted away from straight.

clue.text: Boundless peace and glory

indicators.note: boundless means without boundaries, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: shalom is the Hebrew word for peace

explanation.surface: Endless peace and glory, like a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: In art a glory is a ring of light round a holy figure's head, the same as a halo.

clue.text: Customer rights over property settled in court

indicators.note: settled in means the property rights sit within the court's letters

parts.note: a lien is a legal right to hold another's property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A customer's rights over a property are settled in a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A client is someone buying a professional's services, a customer.

clue.text: Video ref in Dakar bust-up that's typically seen in Africa

indicators.note: a bust-up is a violent breaking apart, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: VAR is the video assistant referee in football

explanation.surface: A video referee row breaks out in Dakar during an African football match.
explanation.walkthrough: Dakar is the capital of Senegal, which keeps the African theme of the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The aardvark is a burrowing anteater native to Africa, so it is typically seen there.

clue.text: Knievel evacuating Yukon, calling for war?

parts.note: Evel Knievel was the American motorcycle stuntman

indicators.note: evacuating empties Yukon of its middle letters, leaving its outer two

explanation.surface: Knievel leaves the Yukon, calling for war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'War' stands for the novelist Waugh, read as it sounds; his first name, his 'calling', is Evelyn.
explanation.definitionFit: Evelyn Waugh was the English novelist, so Evelyn is the given name one calls him by.

clue.text: Erotic novel featuring naked Turk, lady-in-waiting?

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are made into a new order
naked means stripped of its outer layer, here the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A racy novel features a nude Turk and a lady-in-waiting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A lady-in-waiting attends a queen at court, so she is one example of a courtier.
